containers.name: config
command: echo "$CONFIG_0" | base64 -d > /config/mimir.yaml && echo "$CONFIG_1" | base64 -d > /config/loki.yaml && echo "$CONFIG_2" | base64 -d > /config/tempo-backend.yaml

writtenConfigs.loki.yaml:
# Loki on the control node: a single binary (target: all) with its compactor idle (issue 967, D5).
#
# `target: all` is the only way one process both writes and reads the S3 index: a target list that
# names the ingester makes the index shipper write-only. `all` includes the compactor, so compaction
# is pushed ten years out, retention is off, and deletion is disabled (the delete API is not served: it answers 404).
# Nothing in this process compacts or deletes a chunk or an index file.
#
# Dollar-brace values are read from the environment (-config.expand-env=true); the Deployment sets
# them from the cluster-config ConfigMap. Never write a dollar-brace in a comment here: the expansion
# reads comments too, and a malformed one stops the process from starting.
target: all

# Native multi-tenancy: every write and query carries the tenant in X-Scope-OrgID.
auth_enabled: true

server:
  http_listen_port: 3100
  grpc_listen_port: 9098
  log_level: info

common:
  # /loki is a hostPath on the control node: the WAL, the index head and the uploader's name
  # survive a pod restart.
  path_prefix: /loki
  replication_factor: 1
  ring:
    kvstore:
      store: inmemory
    instance_addr: 127.0.0.1
  storage:
    s3:
      bucketnames: easy-db-lab-test
      endpoint: s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
      region: us-west-2

storage_config:
  # Chunks land under <prefix>/<tenant>/ and index tables under <prefix>/index/.
  object_prefix: loki
  tsdb_shipper:
    active_index_directory: /loki/tsdb-index
    cache_location: /loki/tsdb-cache
    # Read side: re-list the index in S3 every minute, so other clusters' uploads become readable
    # soon after they land. The index itself uploads on Loki's fixed 15-minute rotation.
    resync_interval: 1m

# A permanent contract of the shared store: every cluster, past and future, must read the same
# periods. New periods may only be appended, never edited or removed.
schema_config:
  configs:
    - from: "2026-01-01"
      store: tsdb
      object_store: s3
      schema: v13
      index:
        prefix: index_
        period: 24h

ingester:
  wal:
    enabled: true
    dir: /loki/wal
    # A graceful stop flushes every chunk in memory to S3.
    flush_on_shutdown: true
  # Flush a chunk once it spans an hour, so a stream that keeps writing reaches S3 within about an hour.
  # This also sets the per-stream out-of-order window to 30 minutes (half this age): a line more
  # than 30 minutes older than its stream's newest line is rejected. The window is wide so that a
  # slow Loki restart does not drop logs. The annotation mirror is not affected: each annotation is
  # a stream of its own.
  max_chunk_age: 1h
  lifecycler:
    # The ingester's name is part of every index file it uploads, so each file names its tenant and
    # cluster, and two clusters in one tenant never write the same file.
    id: compactor.compactor

querier:
  # One query may name several tenants as `a|b`.
  multi_tenant_queries_enabled: true

compactor:
  working_directory: /loki/compactor
  # The compactor waits one full interval before its first run: ten years is never.
  compaction_interval: 87600h
  retention_enabled: false

limits_config:
  # Retention and deletion are off. The IAM deny on loki/ backs this up.
  retention_period: 0s
  deletion_mode: disabled
  # Accept a year-old line (a backdated annotation, a replayed log) and a day into the future.
  reject_old_samples: true
  reject_old_samples_max_age: 8760h
  creation_grace_period: 24h
  # Every OTLP resource attribute but these four stays structured metadata. `source` is moved onto
  # the resource by the collector so it can be a label.
  otlp_config:
    resource_attributes:
      attributes_config:
        - action: index_label
          attributes:
            - cluster
            - host.name
            - node_role
            - source
  # The defaults are sized for shared SaaS tenants; past them Loki answers a push with a 4xx and
  # the collector drops the batch. They are set far above what a test cluster sends.
  ingestion_rate_mb: 64
  ingestion_burst_size_mb: 128
  per_stream_rate_limit: 32MB
  per_stream_rate_limit_burst: 64MB
  max_global_streams_per_user: 0
  max_label_names_per_series: 30
  max_label_value_length: 16384
  max_query_series: 100000
  max_entries_limit_per_query: 100000
  max_query_length: 0
writtenConfigs.mimir.yaml:
# Mimir on the control node: it writes to the shared store and reads the whole of it (issue 970).
#
# The ingester ships every block to S3 about a minute after cutting it and keeps local blocks for 15
# minutes. The store-gateway answers every query from S3 as well, for every tenant in the account
# bucket, so other clusters' and past runs' metrics are readable here. It finds blocks through each
# tenant's bucket index, which only the account compactor writes. No compactor runs in this process,
# so nothing here can compact, expire, clean up or delete a block, a bucket index, or a tenant.
#
# Queries are not sharded, and readers stop opening a block the compactor merged away soon after its
# deletion mark (issue 988): on this one process both made dashboard loads several times faster.
# The store-gateway's index, chunks and metadata and the query-frontend's results are cached in the
# memcached sidecar on 127.0.0.1:11211, and S3 connections stay open for reuse (issue 988).
#
# Dollar-brace values are read from the environment (-config.expand-env=true); the Deployment sets
# them from the cluster-config ConfigMap. Never write a dollar-brace in a comment here: the expansion
# reads comments too, and a malformed one stops the process from starting.
target: distributor,ingester,querier,query-frontend,query-scheduler,store-gateway

# Native multi-tenancy: every write and query carries the tenant in X-Scope-OrgID. Tenant federation
# lets one query name several tenants as `a|b`; each series then carries __tenant_id__.
multitenancy_enabled: true
tenant_federation:
  enabled: true

server:
  http_listen_port: 9009
  grpc_listen_port: 9097
  log_level: info

# Mimir writes a small activity log for crash diagnosis; keep it on the data volume rather than
# the image's working directory.
activity_tracker:
  filepath: /data/metrics-activity.log

blocks_storage:
  backend: s3
  # The metrics root, mimir, at the top level of the account bucket. Mimir makes one directory per
  # tenant under it.
  storage_prefix: mimir
  s3:
    bucket_name: easy-db-lab-test
    endpoint: s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
    region: us-west-2
    # Keep S3 connections open and reuse them: with the defaults 23% of Mimir's CPU went to new TLS
    # handshakes with S3 (issue 988). 0 is no limit on idle connections in total.
    http:
      idle_conn_timeout: 10m
      max_idle_connections: 0
      max_idle_connections_per_host: 1000
  tsdb:
    # The head, its WAL and every local block live on the control node's disk (a hostPath), so a
    # pod restart replays the WAL and keeps the blocks.
    dir: /data/tsdb
    # One-minute blocks, so a sample reaches S3 in about 2 minutes and other clusters can read it.
    # The ingester cuts a range once a sample later than 1.5 ranges past its start arrives, checked
    # every head_compaction_interval, and the shipper uploads every ship_interval. A 1m range is
    # experimental and hidden in Mimir 3.2.1, which does not validate it.
    block_ranges_period: [1m]
    head_compaction_interval: 15s
    ship_interval: 15s
    # A head with no writes for 2 minutes is compacted, so the last partial block still ships.
    head_compaction_idle_timeout: 2m
    # Local blocks stay for 15 minutes; older ones are read from S3 through the store-gateway. At 2h
    # the ingester kept 366 one-minute blocks and a 1h query opened about 160 of them; at 15m it keeps
    # about 46, its share of Mimir CPU fell from 36% to 10%, and a two-user System Overview load at 1h
    # from 14.7 s to 10.6 s, with no sample lost (issue 988). Mimir requires this to exceed the block
    # range and querier.query_store_after, and it must outlast the store-gateway finding a shipped
    # block (15s ship + 1m bucket index + 1m sync). It removes only local copies already in S3.
    retention_period: 15m
    # A graceful stop compacts the head into a block and ships it.
    flush_blocks_on_shutdown: true
  bucket_store:
    # The store-gateway's index headers, on the control node's disk.
    sync_dir: /data/tsdb-sync
    # New blocks and tenants appear in queries within a minute of the compactor's index update.
    sync_interval: 1m
    ignore_blocks_within: 0
    # Stop reading a block the compactor merged away soon after its deletion mark, rather than for
    # up to an hour. With the compactor's 10-minute first level this cut the tiny blocks per read
    # from ~180 to ~46 (issue 988). They only choose what queries read; the compactor owns deletion.
    ignore_deletion_mark_delay: 10m
    ignore_deletion_mark_while_querying_delay: 5m
    # The store-gateway caches what it reads from S3 in the memcached sidecar, so a dashboard refresh
    # reads index headers, chunks and bucket metadata from memory instead of S3 again (issue 988).
    index_cache:
      backend: memcached
      memcached:
        addresses: 127.0.0.1:11211
    chunks_cache:
      backend: memcached
      memcached:
        addresses: 127.0.0.1:11211
    metadata_cache:
      backend: memcached
      memcached:
        addresses: 127.0.0.1:11211
      # Entries that change as new data lands are cached for 30s, under the 1m sync. At the 5m default
      # for the bucket index the store-gateway saw new blocks only every 5 minutes, the querier's
      # consistency check failed for them (105 of 2,186 checks on qa971f), and dashboards answered 400
      # and 422. The tenant list (15m default) hid a tenant another cluster had just started, the
      # tenant's block list (5m) hid its new blocks, and a meta.json looked up just before its upload
      # stayed missing for 5m. Immutable objects (meta.json content, block index attributes, chunks
      # lists) keep their defaults.
      bucket_index_content_ttl: 30s
      tenants_list_ttl: 30s
      tenant_blocks_list_ttl: 30s
      metafile_doesnt_exist_ttl: 30s
    bucket_index:
      # About 10 years: a stopped compactor leaves the index stale, and that must never fail a query.
      # A tenant with no bucket index returns no stored data rather than an error.
      max_stale_period: 87600h

# Every ring is in this one process: in memory, one replica.
querier:
  # Every query reads the store as well as the ingester, however recent.
  query_store_after: 0
  ring:
    kvstore:
      store: inmemory
    instance_addr: 127.0.0.1

ingester:
  ring:
    kvstore:
      store: inmemory
    replication_factor: 1
    instance_addr: 127.0.0.1
    final_sleep: 0s
    min_ready_duration: 0s

store_gateway:
  sharding_ring:
    kvstore:
      store: inmemory
    replication_factor: 1
    instance_addr: 127.0.0.1

distributor:
  ring:
    kvstore:
      store: inmemory
    instance_addr: 127.0.0.1
  ha_tracker:
    kvstore:
      store: inmemory

# Mimir starts its gossip listener even though no ring uses it. The pod shares the control node's
# network, where Pyroscope already holds the default 7946, so it listens on loopback on its own port.
memberlist:
  bind_addr: [127.0.0.1]
  bind_port: 7947

frontend:
  # The query-scheduler runs in this process.
  scheduler_address: 127.0.0.1:9097
  # Query results are cached in the memcached sidecar, so a refresh reuses the parts of a range it
  # already answered (issue 988). The query engine's range vector splitting cache stays off: Mimir
  # 3.2.1 refuses to start with it.
  cache_results: true
  results_cache:
    backend: memcached
    memcached:
      addresses: 127.0.0.1:11211

frontend_worker:
  scheduler_address: 127.0.0.1:9097

query_scheduler:
  # The query-frontend splits each query by day (query sharding is off), and queues up to 14 parts of it
  # at once (max_query_parallelism). The heaviest dashboard sends about 150 queries in one load, so
  # a load can queue about 2100 parts, which the 8 querier workers drain slowly. Past this limit the
  # scheduler answers 429 and the panel fails. The default of 100 fails most of such a dashboard;
  # 5000 holds two full loads at once.
  max_outstanding_requests_per_tenant: 5000

limits:
  # Cached query results expire after 1h: at the 7-day default a result cached while the compactor lagged kept its gap for days.
  results_cache_ttl: 1h
  # 0 = every query goes to the ingester, however far back.
  query_ingesters_within: 0
  # No query sharding. On one Mimir process it split each query into ~20 parts; turning it off cut
  # Mimir CPU per System Overview load at 1h from 238 s to 66 s (issue 988).
  query_sharding_total_shards: 0
  # The defaults are sized for shared SaaS tenants. Past them Mimir answers the collector's remote
  # write with a 4xx and the batch is dropped, not retried, so they are set far above what a test
  # cluster sends.
  ingestion_rate: 10000000
  ingestion_burst_size: 20000000
  max_global_series_per_user: 0
  max_global_series_per_metric: 0
  max_global_metadata_per_user: 0
  max_global_metadata_per_metric: 0
  max_global_exemplars_per_user: 100000
  max_label_names_per_series: 100
  max_label_name_length: 1024
  max_label_value_length: 16384
  max_fetched_chunks_per_query: 0
  max_fetched_series_per_query: 0
  max_fetched_chunk_bytes_per_query: 0
  # Scrapes and OTLP pushes from several nodes arrive slightly out of order.
  out_of_order_time_window: 10m
writtenConfigs.tempo-backend.yaml:
# Tempo 3.0.3's backend-scheduler and backend-worker in the account compactor (issue 970).
#
# Tempo 3 runs one target per process, so the task runs this file twice: once as the scheduler
# (-target=backend-scheduler) and once as the worker (-target=backend-worker, with its own ports).
# The worker compacts every tenant's blocks under the traces root of the account bucket.
#
# Compaction is on; retention and every other deletion path are off. Tempo has no "retention off"
# once compaction runs, and a zero block retention makes every block eligible for deletion at once,
# so an unreachable retention (100 years) is the off switch. Do not add a per-tenant retention
# override.
#
# Dollar-brace values are read from the environment (-config.expand-env=true); the task definition
# sets them. Never write a dollar-brace in a comment here: the expansion reads comments too.
multitenancy_enabled: true

server:
  http_listen_port: 3200
  grpc_listen_port: 9096

# The scheduler and the worker are separate processes in one task, so each gossips on its own port.
memberlist:
  bind_addr: [127.0.0.1]
  bind_port: 7948

backend_scheduler:
  local_work_path: /var/tempo/scheduler
  provider:
    retention:
      # Retention jobs are scheduled at most once every 10 years; the worker's block retention
      # makes each one a no-op anyway.
      interval: 87600h

backend_worker:
  backend_scheduler_addr: 127.0.0.1:9096
  ring:
    kvstore:
      store: inmemory
    instance_addr: 127.0.0.1
  compaction:
    block_retention: 876000h

storage:
  trace:
    backend: s3
    # Never delete a tenant directory, even one that holds no block.
    empty_tenant_deletion_enabled: false
    wal:
      path: /var/tempo/wal
    s3:
      bucket: easy-db-lab-test
      endpoint: s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
      region: us-west-2
      prefix: tempo

overrides:
  defaults:
    global:
      # 0 = no per-trace size limit, so compaction never drops spans of a large trace.
      max_bytes_per_trace: 0
